P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Under SBV Circular 16/2014/TT-NHNN (in force since 15 Sep 2014; amended by Circular 39/2026/TT-NHNN only for foreign credit institutions' accounts), residents and non-residents, organisations and individuals, may use foreign-currency accounts at licensed banks to receive transfers from abroad. Money can also be moved between their own FX accounts at different banks. No mandatory conversion to VND for individuals was found.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual selling digital products or services register a business? How (sole proprietor), cost, online?
L1_registration.answer: Usually a household business (hộ kinh doanh) registration is needed. Under Art. 82(3) of Decree 168/2025/NĐ-CP (business registration), only certain groups are exempt: farming, fishing and salt-making households, street vendors, itinerant and seasonal traders, and people providing services with LOW INCOME. The low-income level is set by each province's People's Committee, and conditional business lines are always excluded. Exemption therefore depends on your province's threshold. For tax, individuals and household businesses use their 12-digit personal identification number as their tax code (L2).

Whether online freelancers count as 'low-income service providers' depends on the province's decision (not checked). Registration fees and the online procedure were not checked.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax identification number requirement and how to get it
L2_tax_id.answer: Since 1 July 2025 the 12-digit personal identification number (from the national population database / Căn cước) is used INSTEAD of a separate tax code for households, household businesses, business individuals and individuals (Circular 86/2024/TT-BTC). If you had no tax code before 1/7/2025, a household business registers tax together with its business registration. Your name, date of birth and personal ID number must match the national population database.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: How residents' foreign-sourced or digital income is taxed
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Income from content creation on digital platforms (e.g. YouTube) is treated as business income (tax authority answer, July 2026). From 1 January 2026 (Decree 68/2026/NĐ-CP as amended by Decree 141/2026/NĐ-CP of 29 April 2026), household businesses and business individuals with annual revenue up to VND 1 billion pay no VAT and no personal income tax. Above that, PIT follows Article 7 of PIT Law 109/2025/QH15, and the Q&A says PIT is computed on revenue above the threshold. Business individuals with revenue above VND 1 billion must use e-invoices. For revenue up to 31/12/2025 the old VND 100 million threshold applied, with tax on ALL revenue once exceeded.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported services and digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT Law 48/2024/QH15 (from 1 July 2025): exported services are 0% when supplied to foreign organisations or individuals and consumed outside Viet Nam. The conditions (Decree 181/2025/NĐ-CP Art. 18(2)) are a service contract with the foreign party and non-cash payment documents. The tax authority confirmed (July 2026) that a household business providing software services to foreign customers qualifies for 0% if these conditions are met. Household businesses with revenue up to VND 1 billion are not subject to VAT at all (L3). The 0% list also covers digital information content products supplied abroad, with proof of consumption outside Viet Nam.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: E-commerce / consumer-protection law relevant to online sales
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: E-Commerce Law No. 122/2025/QH15 and its Decree 248/2026/NĐ-CP, both in force since 1 July 2026. Intermediary e-commerce platforms must verify sellers' identity before letting them operate. Social networks with commerce features must identify seller accounts. Livestream sellers, including KOLs and KOCs, must be identity-verified before broadcasting. Buyers must be clearly told seller details, prices, origin, and return, warranty and complaint policies.

L7_incentives.question: Government incentives or schemes for IT/digital exporters or freelancers
L7_incentives.answer: (1) No VAT and no PIT for household or individual businesses with revenue up to VND 1 billion a year (Decree 141/2026), one of the highest small-business thresholds found so far. (2) Exported services, including software and digital content consumed abroad, are 0% VAT with a contract and non-cash payment (L4). (3) Using the personal ID number as the tax code removes a separate tax-code step (L2). Industry incentive schemes were not researched.

D1_id_document.question: Name of the national identity document residents use for identity checks
D1_id_document.answer: The Căn cước card (Identity Card Law 2023, in force 1 July 2024; previously 'Căn cước công dân'). It is mandatory for Vietnamese citizens aged 14 and over. Its 12-digit personal identification number doubles as the tax code (L2). Electronic identity runs through VNeID, which the E-Commerce Law uses for seller verification.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (7) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (8) Local official channel: Resident individuals may hold foreign-currency payment accounts to receive transfers from abroad (SBV Circular 16/2014). Payoneer offers personal accounts without a business licence (P2/P5). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
